blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: While LLMs have transformed text generation, standard chat-and-canvas interfaces often reduce human authoring to quite passive supervision, causing review fatigue, over-reliance on AI, and the sidelining of the human role in long-form, source-grounded writing. Prior systems typically address isolated writing phases, leaving comprehensive end-to-end human-LLM collaboration largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce CoWriter, a proactive agentic scheme that adapts expert human (co-)authoring methodologies from cognitive science to flexibly steer the entire writing workflow while actively encouraging the user to engage. In an exploratory user study, compared to a standard LLM baseline, authors using CoWriter better expressed their perspectives and maintained a higher sense of document ownership, supported quantitatively by $2.2\times$ more successful agent engagements. Furthermore, external reader judges rated the resulting texts higher in "human touch" qualities like storytelling and integrating unique personal experiences. Overall, our results demonstrate that proactively engaging users through established human practices is beneficial for effective LLM-supported co-authoring, providing useful methodologies, techniques and insights for future research on collaborative agents.
blocks.zh: 虽然LLMS改变了文本生成方式,但标准聊天和canvas接口往往将人类的作者化为相当被动的监督,导致审查疲劳,过度依赖AI,在长形式,源头基础的写作中将人类角色放在一边. 先前的系统一般处理孤立的写作阶段,使得全面的端对端人-LLM合作基本上没有得到探讨. 在本文中,我们引入了CoWriter,这是一种主动的代理计划,它从认知科学中调整了专家的(共同)作者方法,以灵活地引导整个写作工作流程,同时积极鼓励用户参与. 与标准的LLM基线相比,在一项探索性用户研究中,使用CoWriter的作者更好地表达了他们的观点,并保持了更高的文件所有权感,在数量上得到了2.2美元更成功的代理业务的支持。 此外,外部读者评委将由此产生的文字评为"人类触摸"的品质更高,如讲故事和融合独特的个人经历. 总体而言,我们的成果表明,通过既定的人类做法,主动让用户参与,有利于由LLM支持的有效共同撰写,为今后关于协作代理人的研究提供有用的方法、技术和见解。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Writing has been a fundamental human activity for millennia. Recently, though, Large Language Models (LLMs) have reshaped how we create texts, making LLM-assisted writing one of the most widespread uses of these models ( Chatterji et al., 2025 ) .
Nowadays, authors increasingly rely on LLMs, through standard chat or interactive canvas interfaces, to alleviate demanding authoring tasks like synthesizing sources and drafting large blocks of content ( Mysore et al., 2025 ) .
LLMs now significantly lower the writing barrier with fast, fluent text generation, empowering a diverse range of users to compose complex, multi-page documents.
blocks.zh:
写作是人类几千年来的一项基本活动. 最近,大语言模型(LLMs)重新塑造了我们创建文本的方式,使得LLM辅助写作成为这些模型最广泛的用途之一(Chatterji等人,2025年).
如今,作者越来越多地依靠LLMs,通过标准聊天或交互式画布接口,减轻像合成源和起草大量内容块这样的要求作者的任务(Mysore等人,2025年).
LLMS现在以快速,流利的文本生成方式大幅降低写作屏障,授权不同范围的用户编写复杂的多页文档.

blocks.en:
Yet, such LLM-boosted text generation often comes at the expense of sidelining the human role and effectiveness in the authoring process. This comes with over-reliance on LLM outputs along with challenges like verifying text faithfulness and review fatigue ( Buçinca et al., 2021 ; Huang et al., 2025 ) .
Indeed, few recent works explored improving human-LLM co-authoring processes, addressing concrete aspects such as pre-writing brainstorming Jiang et al. (2024) , outlining Zhang et al. (2026) and turn-based initiative-taking Shao et al. (2026) .
However, an agentic scheme that actively engages the human throughout the entire co-authoring process, from brainstorming to reviewing, remains under-explored.
blocks.zh:
然而,这种由LLM推动的文本生成往往以牺牲撰写过程中的人的作用和效力为代价。 这伴随着过分依赖LLM产出,以及核查文本的忠实性和审查疲劳症等挑战(Buçinca等人,2021年;Huang等人,2025年)。
事实上,最近很少作品探讨改进人与LLM共同撰写过程,涉及具体方面,如撰写前集思广益的Jiang等人(2024年),概述Zhang等人(2026年)和回合倡议的Shao等人(2026年)。
然而,从集思广益到审查等整个共同起草过程中积极吸收人类参与的代理计划仍然没有得到充分利用。

blocks.en:
In this paper, we propose a novel approach towards bridging these gaps in the complex setting of long-form, source-grounded authoring.
Our research hypothesis is that effective synergetic human-LLM co-authoring may be achieved by properly adapting established expert methodologies for human-human co-authoring.
To explore it, we present CoWriter , an agentic scheme following the seminal cognitive-science work of Flower and Hayes (1981) and its prominent extension to writing teams by Lowry et al. (2004) . These works formalize distinct writing activities (such as brainstorming, outlining, drafting, and reviewing) and, for teams, collaborator roles (e.g., leaders, writers, and reviewers).
Our adaptation steers the writing process flexibly through these activities, while keeping the human author fully engaged and influential all along.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们提出了一个新颖的办法,在长形式、以来源为基础的写作的复杂环境中弥补这些差距。
我们的研究假设是,可以通过适当调整既定的人类-人类共同撰写专家方法,实现有效的协同人类-LLM合著。
为了探索它,我们介绍了CoWriter,这是继Flower和Hayes(1981年)的开创性认知科学工作之后的代理计划,以及Lowry等人(2004年)对写作团队的突出延伸。 这些工作将不同的写作活动正规化(如集思广益、概述、起草和审查),对于团队来说,合作者的角色(如领导人、作家和审查者)。
我们的适应通过这些活动灵活地指导着写作过程,同时始终使人类作者充分参与和有影响力。

blocks.en: The key component of our co-authoring framework (§ 3 ) is an agentic lead co-author that guides the writing process through the methodology’s activities, while letting both authors move between them flexibly. Throughout the process, the agent keeps the human co-author engaged and in control of shaping perspectives, steering the narrative, and verifying claims. Following these methodologies, our scheme includes a monitoring component that oversees the writing progress and keeps the lead agent aligned with the methodical workflow, and a “fresh” reviewer agent that provides objective external feedback, unbiased by the writing history.
blocks.zh: 我们共同作者框架的关键组成部分(第3节)是一个代理主导共同作者,通过方法活动指导写作过程,同时让两位作者灵活地在他们之间行动。 在整个过程中,代理人一直让人类共同作者参与并控制观点的塑造,引导叙事,核实说法. 按照这些方法,我们的计划包括一个监测部分,监督编写进度,使牵头代理人与方法性工作流程保持一致,以及一个“新鲜”审查员代理人,提供客观的外部反馈,不受编写历史的偏见。

blocks.en:
To assess the utility of CoWriter for human users, we devise a comprehensive evaluation scheme that involves author-centric assessments alongside objective measurements of the co-authoring session trajectories (e.g., writing-activity coverage and user engagement) and the eventual written document.
In our experiments, 14 participants each co-authored a document once with our agentic system and once with a typical baseline setting involving a frontier LLM chat, canvas and source documents.
Notably, with CoWriter , authors felt substantially more comfortable and engaged throughout the authoring process and more successful in expressing their own perspectives, leading to a much higher sense of ownership of the final document.
Further, CoWriter elicited about twice as many successful agent engagements as the baseline LLM setting.
From an external reader’s assessment, documents produced with CoWriter were found to be more appealing in “human touch” quality aspects, such as expressing unique ideas and the author’s personal experience, storytelling and being more naturally read.
blocks.zh:
为了评估CoWriter对人类用户的效用,我们设计了一个全面的评价计划,其中包括以作者为中心的评估,同时对共同作者的会话轨迹进行客观的测量(如写作活动覆盖面和用户参与)以及最终的书面文件.
在我们的实验中,14名参与者各自与我们的代理系统共同撰写了一份文件,并有一次有典型的基准设定,涉及前沿LLM聊天、帆布和源文件。
值得注意的是,与CoWriter合作,作者在撰写过程中感到更加舒适和参与,在表达自己的观点方面更加成功,从而导致对最后文件的主人翁感大大提高。
此外,CoWriter吸引了大约两倍于LLM基线设定的成功代理人参与。
根据外部读者的评估,与CoWriter一起编写的文件被认为在 " 人类接触 " 质量方面更具吸引力,如表达独特的思想和作者的个人经历、讲故事和更自然地阅读。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Human-LLM Co-Authoring
blocks.zh: 2.1 人体-LLM 共同授权

blocks.en: Assisting humans to write and express knowledge has long been a research goal, predating LLMs by decades ( Engelbart, 1962 ) . Unlike fully automatic text generation, human–LLM co-authoring combines the strengths of LLMs with human contributions, perspectives, and editorial control.
blocks.zh: 协助人类写作和表达知识,长期以来一直是一项研究目标,比法学硕士提前几十年(Engelbart,1962年)。 与全自动文本生成不同,人-LLM合写结合了LLMs的优点与人的贡献,视角,编辑控制.

blocks.en: Many recent LLM-powered writing assistants focus on inline editor assistance, including autocomplete, rewriting, and local text suggestions ( Yuan et al., 2022 ; Lee et al., 2022 ; Zhang et al., 2023 ; Hoque et al., 2024 ; Yeh et al., 2024 , e.g.,) . These systems are largely orthogonal to our work, as such assistive features can naturally be incorporated into our broader co-authoring scheme.
blocks.zh: 最近许多LLM动力的写作助手都专注于内置编辑协助,包括自动完成,重写,以及本地文本建议(袁等人,2022年;李等人,2022年;张等人,2023年;何克等人,2024年;叶赫等人,2024年等). 这些系统对于我们的工作来说基本上是正统的,因为这些辅助性特征自然可以纳入我们更广泛的共同撰写计划。

blocks.en: Closer to our setting are recent agentic co-authoring systems, in which an LLM actively participates in writing. Jiang et al. (2024) focuses primarily on pre-writing exploration and discovering “unknown unknowns.” Shao et al. (2026) studies turn-based collaborative environments built around a chat interface, shared document canvas, and source materials. Others explore alternative interfaces, such as the tree-structured document representation of Zhang et al. (2026) .
blocks.zh: 离我们的环境更近的是最近的代理合写系统,其中LLM积极参与写作. Jiang et al. (2024年)主要专注于写作前的探索和发现“未知的未知数”。 绍等. (2026)研究围绕聊天界面,共享文档画布,以及源材料构建的回合式合作环境. 其他人则探索替代接口,如张等人的树结构文件代表(2026).

blocks.en: We focus on proactive agentic behavior that orchestrates an established authoring methodology while sustaining user engagement, thereby mitigating the “human-sidelining” effect that writers report ( Zhao et al., 2025 ; Reza et al., 2025 ) . Specifically, our work targets source-grounded factual authoring, which requires continued human involvement in activities such as claim verification, perspective shaping, and narrative steering.
blocks.zh: 我们侧重于主动的代理行为,即协调既定的撰写方法,同时保持用户的参与,从而减轻作者报告的“人为排他”效应(赵等人,2025年;礼萨等人,2025年)。 具体地说,我们的工作目标是基于来源的事实作者,这需要人类继续参与诸如索赔核实、视角塑造和叙事指导等活动。

blocks.en: 2.2 Human (Co-)Authoring Methodologies
blocks.zh: 2.2 人类(共同)授权方法

blocks.en:
Research in cognitive science and collaborative writing has extensively studied how skilled authors operate, providing a strong empirical foundation for our method design.
Single-author writing is widely modeled as an iterative process of planning, translating, and reviewing, coordinated by a central monitor ( Flower and Hayes, 1981 ) , rather than a linear progression toward a final document.
During this process, an expert writer engages in knowledge-transforming , i.e., reshaping content according to goals and audience, rather than simply knowledge-telling ( Bereiter and Scardamalia, 1987 ) .
Specific stages within this process are associated with better documents, including rich initial goal setting to define the task ( Flower and Hayes, 1980 ) , dedicated pre-writing brainstorming ( Graham and Perin, 2007 ) , and formal outlining prior to drafting ( Kellogg, 1988 ) .
blocks.zh:
认知科学和合作写作的研究广泛研究了熟练的作者如何操作,为我们的方法设计提供了强大的经验基础.
单作者写作被广泛作为规划、翻译和审查的迭代过程,由中央监测器协调(Flower and Hayes,1981年),而不是向最后文件的线性进展。
在这一过程中,一位专家作家从事知识转化,即根据目标和受众重塑内容,而不是简单地讲知识(Bereiter和Scardamalia,1987年)。
这一过程的具体阶段与更好的文件有关,包括界定任务的丰富的初始目标设定(Flower and Hayes,1980年),专门的预写集思广益(Graham and Perin,2007年),以及起草前的正式概述(Kellogg,1988年)。

blocks.en: In multi-author settings, poorly organized collaboration often becomes inefficient and frustrating ( Ede and Lunsford, 1990 ) . To structure effective and coherent collaboration, Lowry et al. (2004) synthesized empirical studies of real writing teams into a foundational taxonomy of expert collaborative writing activities and flows. Notably, this taxonomy formalizes distinct activities (brainstorming, outlining, drafting, reviewing, revising, and copyediting) alongside specific roles, such as leaders, writers, and reviewers ( Posner and Baecker, 1992 ) .
blocks.zh: 在多作者环境中,组织不当的合作往往效率低下,令人沮丧(Ede和Lunsford,1990年)。 为组织有效和一致的合作,Lowry等人, (2004年)将真实写作团队的经验性研究综合为专家合作写作活动和流的基本分类. 值得注意的是,这一分类法将不同的活动(集思广益、概述、起草、审查、修订和复制)与领导者、作家和审查者等具体角色一起正式化(Posner和Baecker,1992年)。

blocks.en: Directly operationalizing these expert methodologies, our agentic workflow (§ 3 ) adapts the taxonomy of Lowry et al. (2004) into a structured LLM-based co-authoring workflow, guided by three specialized agentic components.
blocks.zh: 直接运用这些专家方法,我们的代理工作流程(第3节)调整了Lowry等人的分类。 (2004年)成为结构化的LLM合写工作流程,由三个专门的代理组件指导.

blocks.en: 3 CoWriter Co-Authoring Architecture
blocks.zh: 3 联合授权建筑

blocks.en: This section introduces CoWriter , an agent-based platform for the co-authoring task (§ 3.1 ) designed to lead a methodological co-writing process (§ 3.2 ; Figure 1 ). The system includes a main agent to direct the workflow and engage the human co-author (§ 3.3 ; Table 1 ), a monitor to oversee the writing process (§ 3.3.2 ), and a reviewer agent to provide external “objective” feedback (§ 3.4 ). We then deploy CoWriter (§ 4 ) to assess the benefits of this guided approach (§ 5 ).
blocks.zh: 本节介绍CoWriter, 即一个基于代理的平台,用于共同撰写任务(§3.1),旨在领导一个方法共同撰写过程(§ 3.2;图1。 该系统包括一个主要代理人来指导工作流程和与人类共同作者接触(§3.3;表1),一个监督写作过程的监视器(§3.3.2),以及一个提供外部“客观”反馈的审查员代理人(§3.4)。 然后,我们部署CoWriter(第4节)评估这一指导办法的益处(第5节)。

blocks.en: 3.1 CoWriter Task and Environment
blocks.zh: 3.1 作者任务和环境

blocks.en:
We extend the collaborative human-agent authoring task from prior work ( Jiang et al., 2024 ; Shao et al., 2026 ) to a source-grounded setting, where we focus on authoring long documents with explicit structure (i.e., hierarchically titled sections) whose content relies substantially on given (and cited) source documents.
To maintain faithfulness to the sources and enable effective content verification ( Gao et al., 2023 ) , we expect that any information requiring citation (e.g., not insights and perspectives of the author, or functional statements; Zhang et al., 2025 ) would explicitly reference supporting evidence in the source documents.
blocks.zh:
我们把合作的人类代理作者任务从先前的工作(Jiang等人,2024年;Shao等人,2026年)扩大到基于源的设定,集中力量编写具有明确结构的长篇文件(即分级标题的章节),其内容主要依靠给定(和引用)源文件。
为了保持对资料来源的忠实,并能够有效核实内容(Gao等人,2023年),我们期望任何需要引用的信息(如作者的见解和观点,或功能性陈述;Zhang等人,2025年)将在资料来源文件中明确提及佐证证据。

blocks.en:
The CoWriter environment employs an augmented chat-and-canvas layout (left part of Figure 1 ). Similar to standard chat-assisted writing, it includes a chat-based message queue for human-agent communication, and a canvas for joint document authoring. In addition, following Shao et al. (2026) , the UI also includes a source explorer to view information about the source documents (UI screenshot in App. A ).
Notably, the canvas supports concurrent document updates by the user and the agent at any moment. In contrast to turn-based co-authoring approaches ( Shao et al., 2026 ) , this allows the agent to proactively act upon user edits.
blocks.zh:
CoWriter环境采用了增强的聊天和扫描布局(图1左部分)。 与标准聊天辅助写法类似,它包括基于聊天的信息队列用于人代理通信,以及用于联合文档编写工作的画布. 此外,在Shao et al.(2026)之后,UI还包括了一位查看源文件信息的源探索者(App.A中的UI截图).
值得注意的是,画布支持用户和代理商随时同时更新文档. 与回合制合写方式(Shao等人,2026年)形成对比,这使得代理在用户编辑时可以主动采取行动.

blocks.en: 3.2 CoWriter Agentic System Architecture
blocks.zh: 3.2 CoWriter代理系统架构

blocks.en: Table 1: The iterative co-authoring workflow steps (§ 3.3.1 ) encoded in the Leader system prompt (adapted from the writing activities of Lowry et al., 2004 ). The per-step invite instruction specifies how the agent encourages engagement. Colors denote workflow phases ( Figure 1 ): planning , production , finalization , and ad-hoc requests .
blocks.zh: 表1:在Lader系统中编码的迭代合写工作流程步骤(第3.3.1节)(根据Lowry等人的写作活动改编,2004年)。 每一步邀请指令规定了代理人如何鼓励参与。 颜色表示工作流程阶段(图1):规划、生产、定稿和临时请求。

blocks.en:
To translate expert human-human co-authoring dynamics into an agentic architecture ( Yao et al., 2023 ; Guo et al., 2024 ) , we distill collaborative concepts from established writing models ( Flower and Hayes, 1981 ; Lowry et al., 2004 , § 2.2 ;) , mapping the core co-authoring roles directly onto three agentic components: the Leader , Monitor and Reviewer ( Figure 1 , right).
Implemented via system prompts and tool use, these components dynamically accommodate the non-linear iterative nature of human writing rather than enforcing a rigid sequential workflow, as our transition analysis confirms (§ 5.1 ).
blocks.zh:
为了将专家人与人合写动态转化为代理架构(Yao等人,2023年;Guo等人,2024年),我们从既定的写作模式(Flower and Hayes,1981年;Lowry等人,2004年;§2.2;)中提炼出协作概念,将核心合写角色直接映射到三个代理组件:领导者、监测和审查者(图1,右)。
这些组成部分通过系统提示和工具使用加以实施,动态地适应了人类书写的非线性迭代性质,而不是像我们的过渡分析所证实的那样,强制执行僵硬的顺序工作流程(第5.1节)。

blocks.en:
The Leader agent (§ 3.3 ) functions as the process lead Lowry et al. (2004) , fully participating in the writing itself and guiding the workflow while motivating and encouraging the users to be active as well.
To support both the Leader and the user, a separate Monitor component (§ 3.3.2 ) acts as a writing strategist to track overarching progress and dictate transitions between authoring stages Flower and Hayes (1981) .
The Reviewer agent (§ 3.4 ) functions as an on-demand external reviewer , providing feedback on the document free from the inherent biases that both the Leader and the user develop during the writing process.
In this environment, the human collaborator both directly co-authors the text and interacts with the Leader .
blocks.zh:
领导者代理人(第3.3节)作为领导Lowry等人(2004年)的过程,充分参与写作本身并指导工作流程,同时激励和鼓励用户也积极参与。
为了支持领袖和使用者,一个单独的Monitor组件(§ 3.3.2)起到写作战略家的作用,以跟踪总体进展,并规定作者阶段Flower和Hayes之间的过渡(1981年)。
审查者代理(§3.4)发挥点播外部审查者的作用,就文档提供反馈,而不受领导者和使用者在写作过程中形成的固有偏见的影响。
在这样的环境下,人类合作者既直接共同撰写文本,又与领袖互动.

blocks.en: 3.3 Leader Agent
blocks.zh: 3.3 领导代理人

blocks.en: The Leader is the primary agentic collaborator — it reads sources and revises the document, while using conversation to proactively guide and engage the user through the co-authoring workflow.
blocks.zh: 领导者是主要的代理合作者——它读取源头并修改文档,同时利用对话来主动引导和通过共同编写工作流程接触用户.

blocks.en: 3.3.1 Core Functionality
blocks.zh: 3.3.1 核心功能

blocks.en:
The agent’s core is a 7.7k-token system prompt (full prompt in Figure 28 , App. B ) implementing an agentic workflow that adapts the (human) co-authoring process and writing activities formulated by Lowry et al. (2004) .
Its steps ( 1 – 7 ) are depicted in Table 1 .
blocks.zh:
该代理的核心是7.7k-token系统提示(在图28,App.B中完全提示),执行一种代理工作流程,调整Lowry等人拟定的(人)合写程序和写作活动(2004年)。
其步骤(1-7)见表1。

blocks.en:
Primarily, the Leader is instructed to proactively guide the user through the co-authoring activities, rather than simply following user instructions, as the writing-activity coverage results in § 5.1 show.
At the same time, it is directed to comply with ad hoc user requests even when they deviate from the workflow ( ∗ \ast in Table 1 ).
To facilitate a methodological workflow, 2 2 2 The workflow is laid out in one prompt, and not split to components, to allow flexibility to maneuver between steps non-sequentially. each of the seven steps is defined using structured fields:
(a) step transitions , which define when to trigger the step, the typical number of turns, and possible transitions to other steps;
(b) the goal of the step alongside a series of actions to fulfill it;
(c) environment actions specifying how to interact with the sources, canvas, and chat (e.g., exploring sources or updating the document outline); and
(d) invites , which are proactive suggestions to encourage step-relevant user engagement (see below).
Finally, when the user edits the document, the Leader proactively acts upon the revisions rather than waiting for explicit instructions.
For example, renaming an entity in the text will trigger the Leader (via the Monitor ; § 3.3.2 ) to proactively update the remaining entity mentions throughout the document.

To promote user engagement and prevent the human from being sidelined in the co-authoring process, the per-step invite instructions specify targeted step-relevant actions to encourage participation (right column of Table 1 ). The agent adapts its invitations to the current step by asking questions, proposing alternatives, requesting feedback, or soliciting the user’s own ideas.
Complementarily, when handling ad hoc user requests, the prompt instructs the agent to finish each turn with a follow-up option related to the request, alongside an option to return (or proceed) to the most appropriate workflow step.
For example, if a user asks about information in the sources, the agent might offer to incorporate the resulting insight into the document or alternatively to move on to the next step.
To further restrain the LLM from sidelining the user, the agent is directed to maintain a conversational cadence through short bite-sized interactions and incremental document updates, manageable for the human co-author. To assist the user in tracing source information, the agent anchors claims via citations to specific source spans rather than to full documents ( Slobodkin et al., 2024 ; Hirsch et al., 2025 ) .
Finally, the user is kept engaged via an updated Writing Log widget, maintained by the Monitor , that displays the current process state (example in Figure 21 , App. C ).
blocks.zh:
为了促进用户参与,防止人在共同撰写过程中被置于一边,每一步邀请指示具体说明有针对性的与步骤有关的行动,以鼓励参与(表1右栏)。 代理商通过提问、提出替代方案、要求反馈或征求用户自己的想法来调整其邀请。
作为补充,在处理临时用户请求时,即时指示代理完成每个回合,并附上与请求相关的后续选项,同时选择返回(或继续)最适当的工作流程步骤。
例如,如果用户询问信息来源中的信息,代理人可以提出将由此产生的见解纳入文件,或者转而采取下一步。
为了进一步限制LLM让用户靠边,该代理被指示通过短咬大小的相互作用和递增文件更新来保持对话的cadence,对于人类共同作者来说是可以管理的. 为了协助用户追踪来源信息,代理商通过引用特定来源的长度而不是完整的文件(Slobodkin等人,2024年;Hirsch等人,2025年)。
最后,用户通过一个更新的写入日志部件(由Monitor维护)继续参与,该部件显示当前的进程状态(例如图21,App.C)。

blocks.en: 3.3.2 The Monitor

During complex authoring processes, both human writers and LLM-based agents can drift off-track, necessitating a governing element. To maintain focus, human cognitive models describe a central monitor ( Flower and Hayes, 1981 ) , and recent agentic systems employ mechanisms to moderate the process ( Jiang et al., 2024 ; Balepur et al., 2025 ) . Inspired by these concepts, the Monitor is an LLM-based component embedded within the Leader . It observes environment events — such as document updates and user messages — and tracks progress along the workflow steps.
blocks.zh: 在复杂的撰写过程中,人类作家和基于LLM的代理人都可能偏离轨道,因此需要一个管理要素。 为了保持焦点,人类的认知模型描述了一个中央显示器(Flower and Hayes,1981年),而最近的代理系统采用了机制来调节这一过程(Jiang等人,2024年;Balepur等人,2025年)。 在这些概念的启发下,“监测”是一个基于LLM的组件,嵌入在“领导”中。 它观察环境活动——如文件更新和用户信息——并跟踪工作流程步骤的进展情况。

blocks.en:
To maintain visibility of the workflow progress, the Monitor maintains a Writing Log widget (example in App. C ), providing structured context to both the user and the agent. The log displays:
(a) a checklist of visited workflow steps ( Table 1 );
(b) the explicit writing goal captured from the user; and
(c) a concise timeline of events occurring during the session.
3.4 Reviewer Agent
blocks.zh: 3.4 审查员代理

blocks.en: Delegating critique to a separate agent follows prior multi-agent writing systems that decouple generation from review to reduce confirmation bias and identify a broader range of issues ( Bae and Kim, 2024 ; Hong et al., 2024 ) . In the collaborative-writing taxonomy of Lowry et al. (2004) , a reviewer evaluates the document without participating in its writing. Accordingly, Reviewer simulates an external reviewer from the target audience.
blocks.zh: 将批评委托给一个单独的代理人遵循之前的多代理书写系统,这些系统将生成与审查脱钩,以减少确认偏差,并找出更广泛的问题(Bae和Kim,2024;Hong等人,2024)。 在Lowry等人的合作写作分类法(2004年)中,一名审查员在不参与编写的情况下评价该文件。 因此,审查员模拟来自目标受众的外部审查员。

blocks.en: Invoked on demand by Leader , Reviewer reads only the current document and the Writing Goal section of the Writing Log . It does not access the chat history or activity log, making its feedback independent of the authoring process. The agent can additionally retrieve relevant source content to verify claims or identify missing information.
blocks.zh: 评论员根据领袖的要求, 它不访问聊天历史或活动日志,使其反馈独立于作者进程. 代理人可以额外检索相关的源内容,以核实索赔或识别缺失的信息.

blocks.en: Reviewer returns a concise structured review containing bulleted lists of strengths , issues , and suggested fixes . Leader then surfaces the review in the chat for collaborative action. Additional technical details are provided in App. E .
blocks.zh: 评论员返回一份简洁的结构审查,其中载有各种长处、问题和建议的纠正办法。 领导者然后在聊天中浮出评论来进行协作行动. 附录E提供了其他技术细节。

blocks.en: 4 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4 实验设置

blocks.en: Our experiments evaluate whether guiding users through a methodical workflow leads to an effective collaborative writing process and produces a source-grounded document that users can confidently approve. We describe our user study comparing CoWriter against a baseline (§ 4.1 ), followed by our evaluation dimensions for both the co-authoring sessions and the final outputs (§ 4.2 ).
blocks.zh: 我们的实验评价通过方法性工作流程指导用户是否导致有效的合作写作过程,并产生一个基于源的文件,用户可以有信心地批准. 我们介绍我们的用户研究,比较CoWriter与基线(§4.1),然后是共同编写会议和最后产出的评价层面(§4.2)。

blocks.en: 4.1 User Study Design
blocks.zh: 4.1 用户研究设计

blocks.en: The study simulates a realistic long-form writing task requiring prolonged human-agent interaction. Participants collaboratively authored a 750–1000 word blog post on a specified topic, grounded in provided sources. To elicit meaningful, active user contributions, we instructed participants to act as a popular blogger , tasking them with combining factual claims from the sources with their own perspectives , personal experiences , and illustrative examples (full details in App. F ).
blocks.zh: 该研究模拟了一个现实的长形写作任务,需要人类与物剂的长期互动. 参与者合作撰写了750-1 000字博客文章, 我们指示参与者做一个受欢迎的博客, 要求他们将来自来源的实事求是的说法与自己的观点、个人经历和说明性例子(详情见App.

blocks.en:
We adapted four everyday-life blog topics from the DREsS dataset ( Yoo et al., 2025 ) (e.g., “The Impact of Smartphones on Family and Friend Communication” ), manually chosen to satisfy three criteria: (i) they are easy to understand and sufficiently engaging for non-expert writers, (ii) all topics encourage participants to contribute personal perspectives and experiences, and (iii) they are comparable in complexity and writing difficulty.
For each topic, we manually curated ten relevant diverse academic research papers. To keep the reading load manageable, each source was required to be academically credible, relevant, permissively licensed, and under 20 pages (see App. G ).
blocks.zh:
我们改编了DREsS数据集(Yoo等人,2025年)(例如“智能手机对家庭和朋友交流的影响”)的四个日常生活博客主题,这些主题是为了满足三个标准而人工选择的:(一) 这些主题对非专家作家来说是容易理解和充分参与的;(二) 所有主题都鼓励参与者提供个人观点和经验;(三) 它们在复杂性和写作困难方面是可比较的。
对于每个课题,我们手动整理了十篇相关的多种学术研究论文. 为了保持阅读负荷的可控性,每个来源必须具有学术可信性、相关性和许可性,并低于20页(见附录G)。

blocks.en:
We compared CoWriter against a control baseline that simulates a standard LLM-assisted setup of a chat, a document canvas, and uploaded sources, excluding the components supporting our co-authoring workflow and user engagement.
To ensure a fair comparison, both systems share the exact same environment and underlying model. 3 3 3 All systems and agents run on a claude-sonnet-4.6 backbone model with low thinking effort, to balance performance and response time. To mitigate possible confounding variables, we stripped our collaborative mechanisms: we modified the Leader prompt to remove the workflow and engagement instructions, and disabled the other two agentic components, the Writing Log , and localized attribution.
blocks.zh:
我们比较了CoWriter与一个控制基线,该控制基线模拟了一个标准的LLM辅助的聊天设置,一个文件画布,以及上传的源,不包括支持我们共同编写的工作流程和用户参与的组件.
为确保进行公平的比较,两个系统都具有完全相同的环境和基本模式。 3 3 3 所有系统和特工都运行在低思量的claude-sonnet-4.6主干模型上,以平衡性能和反应时间. 为了减少可能出现的混乱变量,我们取消了我们的合作机制:我们修改了“领袖”的提示,删除了工作流程和接触指令,并取消了另外两个代理组件,即“写日志”和本地化属性。

blocks.en: Fourteen graduate students with academic writing experience participated in a within-subjects study. 4 4 4 We conducted a 3-participant pilot prior to the full study to refine the system and experimental protocol. Following an orientation and 15 minutes of guided practice per system, participants completed two writing sessions on different topics — one with CoWriter and one with the baseline. To encourage realistic iterative writing and source exploration, each session was intended to last up to 75 minutes, with the second session occurring within 48 hours of the first. We counterbalanced both the system order and the topic-to-system assignment, ensuring that all topics appeared approximately equally often in both conditions. Participants completed post-session questionnaires after each task, followed by a final comparative survey upon finishing both. Recruitment and procedural details are in App. H .
blocks.zh: 14名有学术写作经验的研究生参加了学科内的研究. 4 4 4,我们在全面研究完善制度和实验规程之前,进行了3人参与试点. 在每次系统进行情况介绍和15分钟的导游练习后,学员们完成了两次关于不同专题的写作会议——一次与CoWriter,一次与基线。 为了鼓励现实的迭代写作和源头探索,每场会议都打算持续长达75分钟,第二场会议将在第一次会议之后的48小时内举行。 我们平衡了系统顺序和专题对系统分配,确保所有专题在两种条件下都大致相同地出现。 与会者在完成每项任务后填写了会后调查表,然后在完成这两项任务后进行最后比较调查。 征聘和程序细节载于App.H。

blocks.en: 4.2 Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4.2 评价

blocks.en: A comprehensive evaluation of co-authoring requires assessing the system’s impact on both the writing process and the user, rather than just the final text. Accordingly, we evaluate sessions across two dimensions: (1) the authoring process , focusing on workflow adherence, user engagement, and process efficiency; and (2) the produced document , focusing on output quality and human author expression. For both dimensions, we utilize authors’ questionnaire ratings alongside quantitative measurements and external judgments. This section outlines these aspects; full results are in § 5 .
blocks.zh: 对共同作者的全面评价要求评估系统对写作过程和用户的影响,而不仅仅是最后文本。 因此,我们从两个方面评价会议:(1) 编写过程,重点是工作流程遵守、用户参与和进程效率;(2) 编写的文件,重点是产出质量和作者的表达。 在这两个方面,我们利用作者的问卷评级以及定量衡量和外部判断。 本节概述了这些方面;全部结果载于第5节。

blocks.en:
To capture user preference and perception, our evaluation relies on a comparative questionnaire. After completing both sessions, participants answered 13 questions on a 5-point scale (ranging from “Prefer System A” to “Prefer System B”), eliciting pairwise preferences on user engagement, the authoring process, output quality, and confidence in the final document.
To corroborate these comparative results, participants also completed per-session questionnaires after each task. These measured similar aspects while incorporating standard instruments for cognitive load (adapted from NASA-TLX; Hart and Staveland, 1988 ) and usability ( Finstad, 2010 ) . We observed consistent trends across both questionnaire formats (questions and details in App. I ).
blocks.zh:
为了了解用户的偏好和看法,我们的评价依赖于比较问卷。 在完成这两场会议之后,与会者以5分比例(从“优先系统A”到“优先系统B”)回答了13个问题,从而在用户参与、编写过程、产出质量和对最后文件的信心方面获得双向偏好。
为了证实这些比较结果,与会者在每项任务之后还完成了每次会议的调查问卷。 这些测量了类似的方面,同时纳入了认知负载的标准仪器(改编自NASA-TLX;Hart and Staveland,1988年)和使用性(Finstad,2010年)。 我们注意到两种问卷格式的一致趋势(问题和详情载于附录一)。

blocks.en: To quantitatively assess the process efficiency, we measure standard effort indicators: elapsed time, number of turns and quantity of generated tokens. Furthermore, we introduce three novel metrics to evaluate the quality of the collaboration.
blocks.zh: 为了从数量上评估过程效率,我们衡量标准的努力指标:时间过长、转弯次数和生成信号的数量。 此外,我们采用三个新的衡量标准来评估合作的质量。

blocks.en: (1) Coverage of writing activities measures a system’s proactive effort to encourage collaboration through the seven writing activities defined in the co-authoring workflow (§ 2.2 ; Table 1 ). It is estimated per activity as the percentage of sessions that include it. To derive these percentages, an LLM 5 5 5 We annotated both writing activities and engagement using claude-opus-4.8 with high reasoning effort. Inter-rater agreement with two human annotators on a 118-message subset yielded an average Cohen’s κ = 0.54 \kappa=0.54 , detailed in App. K . labels each turn in each session with one of the seven activities or ‘other’.
blocks.zh: (1) 写作活动的涵盖范围衡量一个系统的积极努力,通过共同编写工作流程中界定的七项写作活动鼓励合作(第2.2节;表1)。 估计每项活动占包括这些活动的会议的百分比。 为了得出这些百分比,我们用Claude-opus-4.8来说明编写活动和参与情况,并进行了大量推理。 与两个人类注释员就118个消息子集达成的协议平均得出Cohen = 0.54 \ kappa = 0.54,详见App. K.

blocks.en: (2) Engagement rate measures the number of engagement expressions per 100 words of agent messages, accommodating systems of different verbosity. To quantify this, an LLM 5 marks all phrases within agent turns that express engagement, defined as either a question , a set of options to choose from, an action request , or a next-step proposal .
blocks.zh: (2) 业务约定率衡量每100字代理信息中的业务约定表达数,容纳不同动词的系统. 为了量化这一点,一个LLM 5标记了代理商转动中表达业务约定的所有短语,定义为:一个问题、一组选择方案、一个行动请求、或者下一个步骤提案。

blocks.en: (3) Successful engagement ratio measures the system’s effectiveness in maintaining user participation. Quantitative engagement metrics in prior work generally focused on the system’s initiations, overlooking the user’s response ( Wu et al., 2025 ; Shao et al., 2026 ) . To capture it, the annotating LLM also marks whether the subsequent user-turns directly respond to each expression. The success ratio is the percentage of engagement expressions that induced a direct user response.
blocks.zh: (3) 成功参与比率衡量系统在维持用户参与方面的效力。 以往工作中的定量参与指标一般侧重于系统的启动,忽略了用户的反应(Wu等人,2025年;Shao等人,2026年)。 为了捕捉它,注释的LLM也标记了后续的用户转动是否直接响应每个表达式. 成功率是导致用户直接反应的接触表达方式的百分比。

blocks.en: Finally, we evaluate the produced texts on four dimensions adapted from Lee et al. (2025) : linguistic fluency, interestingness, logical fluency, and coherence. Both human raters and LLM judges score each text (see App. L ).
blocks.zh: 最后,我们评价从Lee等人(2025年)改编出来的四个方面:语言流利、有趣、逻辑流利和一致性。 人评分和LLM评分都得分每个文本(见App.L.

blocks.en: 5 Results and Analysis
blocks.zh: 5 结果和分析

blocks.en:
We next compare CoWriter to the baseline system in terms of guiding the writing process and maintaining user engagement (§ 5.1 ), process efficiency (§ 5.2 ), and the quality of the authored documents (§ 5.3 ).
Despite the modest cohort size, clear trends stand out, with multiple statistically significant results (detailed results in App. M ).
blocks.zh:
接下来,我们将CoWriter与基线系统进行比较,从指导编写过程和保持用户参与(第5.1节)、程序效率(第5.2节)和编写文件的质量(第5.3节)等方面进行对比。
尽管组群规模不大,但明显的趋势突出,在统计上有多种显著结果(详细结果见App.M)。

blocks.en: 5.1 Workflow Guidance via User Engagement
blocks.zh: 5.1 通过用户参与提供工作流程指导

blocks.en:
The coverage of writing activities is presented in Figure 2 , portraying the percentage of sessions in which the agent addresses each one of the activities at least once.
Overall, the figure clearly indicates that CoWriter -guided sessions closely follow the established co-writing methodology, unlike the baseline sessions guided by a “bare” LLM.
Notably, CoWriter provoked many more sessions with goal-setting (+86%), brainstorming (+43%), and outlining (+57%) activities, while the baseline agent was consistent only with the two straightforward activities of drafting and localized reviewing & revising .
blocks.zh:
图2显示了编写活动的范围,说明了代理人至少一次讨论每项活动的会议的百分比。
总体而言,该图清楚地表明,由CoWriter指导的会议密切遵循既定的共同编写方法,与由“简易”LLM指导的基准会议不同。
值得注意的是,CoWriter在设定目标(+86%)、集思广益(+43%)和概述活动(+57%)方面引发了更多的会议,而基线代理人只与起草和本地化审查和修订这两项直接活动一致。

blocks.en: Furthermore, an analysis of activity counts reveals that most baseline agent-turns that evoke an activity are localized reviewing & revising (54% vs. 29% for CoWriter ; Figure 14 , left). Meanwhile, CoWriter sessions are more balanced across the workflow and elicit equal or greater user participation across all writing activities ( Figure 14 , right).
blocks.zh: 此外,对活动计数的分析表明,引起某项活动的多数基线代理转折是局部审查和修订(CoWriter54%对29%;图14,左)。 同时,CoWriter课程在工作流程中更加平衡,并促使所有写作活动的用户平等或更大参与(图14,右)。

blocks.en: Finally, we analyzed the direction of transitions between any one of the seven writing activities to another ( Figure 15 ), and observed that both systems facilitate a rich, iterative process featuring roughly a third backward transitions to an earlier activity. While the baseline skips to non-adjacent activities 44% of the time, CoWriter transitions are predominantly to adjacent ones (74%; p = 0.015 p=0.015 ), guiding a more methodical process.
blocks.zh: 最后,我们分析了七个写作活动中任何一个向另一个写作活动过渡的方向(图15),并指出,这两个系统都促进一个丰富、迭代的过程,大约是第三个向较早的活动后向过渡。 虽然基准跳过44%的时间为非邻近活动,但CoWriter的过渡主要为邻近活动(74%;p=0.015 p=0.015),指导一个更加有条理的过程.

blocks.en: Figure 2: Percentage of sessions in which each agent (baseline vs. CoWriter ) discussed each of the seven writing activities. Bold bars indicate p < 0.05 p<0.05 significance of CoWriter over the baseline.
blocks.zh: 图 2: 每一代理商(基线与CoWriter)讨论七个写作活动各部分的会议百分比。 粗体条表示CoWriter在基线上的意义 < 0.05 p < 0.05。

blocks.en: Figure 3: Comparative preferences between the baseline and CoWriter by 14 authors (normalized counts). ∗ , ∗∗ , ∗∗∗ denote p < 0.05 , 0.01 , 0.001 p<0.05,0.01,0.001 , respectively.

The first bar in Figure 3 depicts human-author perceived engagement as reported in the pairwise author questionnaire.
Overall, and with high statistical significance, users almost exclusively rated CoWriter as more engaging than the baseline (11 vs. 2; p = 0.006 p=0.006 ).
blocks.zh:
图3中的第一个栏目描绘了双向作者问卷中报告的人类作者认为的参与。
总体而言,而且具有高度统计意义的是,用户几乎完全将CoWriter评为比基线更具参与度(11对2;p=0.006;p=0.006)。

blocks.en:
We observe increased engagement and participation quantitatively as well. CoWriter ’s engagement rate is 0.57 expressions per 100 agent words vs. 0.24 for the baseline ( p = 0.001 p=0.001 ), and its engagements are also more effective, with a successful engagement ratio of 57% vs. 47%. I.e., CoWriter engages the user more frequently and the user cooperates more often, amounting to 235 vs. 109 successful engagement expressions in total ( 2.2 × 2.2\times ).
This advantage in successful engagements consistently holds across engagement types and writing activities ( Figure 16 and Figure 17 , respectively). User -initiated engagements occurred at comparable rates across both systems (2.7 vs. 2.9 per 100 user words), and, unsurprisingly, the agents consistently followed up on them (96%). This demonstrates that CoWriter ’s increased initiative does not diminish user-led interaction.
blocks.zh:
我们看到在数量上也增加了参与。 CoWriter的接触率为每100个代理词0.57个表达式,基线为0.24个(p = 0.001 p = 0.001),它的接触也更为有效,成功接触率为57%对47%. 例如,CoWriter更频繁地与用户接触,用户更频繁地合作,共计235对109次成功接触表达式(2.2×2.2\时)。
这种成功参与的优势始终存在于各种参与类型和写作活动中(分别为图16和图17)。 两个系统都以可比的比率(每100个用户字2.7个对2.9个)进行了用户发起的业务约定,而且毫不奇怪,代理商一直跟踪这些业务(96%)。 这表明CoWriter增加的主动性并不减少用户主导的互动。

blocks.en: Taken together, both the (statistically significant) subjective author perspective and the objective quantification indicate that CoWriter encourages user participation in human-LLM co-writing.
blocks.zh: 综合起来,(具有统计意义的)主观作者观点和客观量化都表明,CoWriter鼓励用户参与人-LLM共同写作.

blocks.en: 5.2 Process Efficiency
blocks.zh: 5.2 过程效率

blocks.en: Next, we observe that even as CoWriter substantially increases user engagement, it is experienced as less cognitively demanding than the baseline (rated 9 vs. 3; 2 in Figure 3 ). 6 6 6 For completeness, App. M reports similar positive trend in NASA-TLX measures ( Hart and Staveland, 1988 ) .
blocks.zh: 其次,我们注意到,即使CoWriter大大增加了用户的参与,其认知要求也低于基线(评级为9对3;图3为2)。

blocks.en:
Additionally, CoWriter demonstrates a somewhat more efficient process with shorter session duration (62 vs. 68 minutes on average).
Quantitative interaction measures (detailed in App. O ) further indicate a more conversational, bite-sized collaboration pattern with CoWriter .
Sessions involved more frequent but shorter interactions (25 vs. 16 agent messages on average, yet 27% fewer total agent words per session), as well as smaller and more frequent document revisions (13 vs. 9 revisions, with 38% fewer added or deleted characters per revision).
Furthermore, CoWriter uses localized citations referencing much smaller source chunks (205 vs. 12,754 average tokens; Zhang et al., 2025 ), easing verification for readers and reviewers, while automatic citation- F 1 F_{1} scores remain high (0.84) for both systems (App. L ).
blocks.zh:
此外,CoWriter还显示出一种效率更高、会期较短的程序(平均62分钟对68分钟)。
量性交互措施(详见App. O)进一步表明与CoWriter(英语:CoWriter)更能对话,咬伤大小的合作模式.
届会涉及更频繁但更短的互动(平均25条对16条代理信息,但每次会议代理词总数减少27%)以及较小和更频繁的文件修订(13条对9条修订,每次修订增加或删除字符减少38%)。
此外,CoWriter使用本地化的引文,引用更小的源块(205对12 754个平均符号;Zhang等人,2025年),方便读者和审查员的核查,而两个系统的自动引文-F 1 F_{1}的分数仍然很高(0.84)(App.L)。

blocks.en: Overall, even though CoWriter provokes more interaction steps, it requires less effort from both the human author and the LLM ( 3 in Figure 3 ), leading 11 participants to prefer it over the baseline for future writing tasks, compared to a single participant preferring the baseline ( p < 0.001 p<0.001 ).
blocks.zh: 总的来说,尽管CoWriter引发了更多的互动步骤,但它要求人类作者和LLM(图3中的3)都付出较少的努力,导致11位参与者倾向于未来写作任务的基线,而一位参与者则倾向于基准(p < 0.001 p < 0.001)。

blocks.en: 5.3 Document Quality
blocks.zh: 5.3 文件质量

blocks.en: We next assess the impact of CoWriter ’s methodological workflow on the quality of the co-authored documents, as evaluated by the participating authors, independent human raters, and LLM judges.
blocks.zh: 我们接下来将评估CoWriter的方法工作流程对共同撰写文件质量的影响,参与的作者、独立的人评分员和LLM法官对此进行了评价。

blocks.en:
The 3 bottom bars of Figure 3 show a clear and statistically significant trend of higher perceived ownership by authors of documents written with CoWriter . This includes self-expression (feeling the text reflected their own style or captured their intended key points), as well as verifiability and integrity (recall CoWriter ’s localized citations, which are easier to verify).
Accordingly, for an overall sense of ownership (willingness to publish the document under the author’s name), 11 participants favored CoWriter , vs. one favoring the baseline ( p = 0.006 p=0.006 ).
In conclusion, documents co-authored with CoWriter are perceived by authors as significantly more authentic to their personal voice, easier to verify, and ultimately more of their own.
blocks.zh:
图3的3条底条显示了一个明显和具有统计意义的趋势,即作者对由CoWriter撰写的文件拥有更多的所有权。 这包括自我表达(认为案文反映了他们自己的风格或抓住了他们想要的关键要点),以及可核查性和完整性(回顾CoWriter的本地引用,比较容易核实)。
因此,为了总的主人翁感(愿意以作者的名义公布文件),11名与会者赞成CoWriter, 而不是赞成基线(p=0.006 p=0.006)。
最后,作者认为,与CoWriter共同编写的文件对其个人声音来说更真实,更容易核实,并最终更真实。

blocks.en: Figure 4: Percentage of pairs preferred per system, rated by five human annotators for the four key dimensions. LLM-as-a-judge counterpart in Figure 11 .
blocks.zh: 图 4:每个系统首选配对的百分比,由5名人类注释员对4个关键维度进行评分. 图11中的LLM-as-a-judge对应数据。

blocks.en:
We employed human and LLM raters to assess the authored documents independently of the co-authoring process, on four key dimensions established in Lee et al. (2025) , depicted in Figure 4 .
Overall, across all four dimensions and the 19 individual evaluation questions, documents co-authored with CoWriter were rated higher than or similarly to those produced with the baseline, which aligns with the authors’ own positive assessments.
blocks.zh:
我们雇用了人和LLM评分员,以图4所描述的李等人(2025年)确立的四个关键层面,独立于共同撰写程序,评估撰写的文件。
总的来说,在所有四个方面和19个个别评价问题中,与CoWriter共同编写的文件的评级高于或类似于与作者自己的积极评价相一致的基准文件。

blocks.en:
Most notably, human raters preferred CoWriter documents for both Linguistic Fluency and Interestingness , with respective preference rates of 43% and 30% higher than for the baseline.
The top five questions favoring CoWriter ( Figure 10 ) mostly relate to author self-expression and a more human writing style, which was also noticeable to external human raters, in sync with authors’ own perceptions. Similar trends appear in the LLM-judge evaluation ( Figure 11 and Figure 12 ), including corresponding preferences for storytelling , use of personal experiences , and unique ideas or perspectives from the author .
blocks.zh:
最值得注意的是,人类评分者偏好语言流利性和趣味性的CoWriter文件,其偏好率分别比基线高43%和30%。
喜欢CoWriter的前五个问题(图10)大多与作者自我表达和较人性化的写作风格有关,这在外部人类的评分中也很明显,与作者自身的认知同步. 类似趋势出现在LLM法官的评价(图11和图12)中,包括讲述故事的相应偏好、个人经验的使用以及作者的独特想法或观点。

blocks.en: These results link the authoring process to document outcomes. A structured process with greater human engagement yields documents that authors and external raters (human and LLM) find more natural and reflective of the author, without sacrificing other quality measures. Human co-writing methods thus transfer well to human-LLM schemes, while human involvement remains valuable.
blocks.zh: 这些成果将编写进程与记录成果联系起来。 由人类更多参与的分阶段进程产生文件,作者和外部评估者(人和LLM)认为这些文件更自然,更能反映作者,同时又不牺牲其他质量措施。 因此,人类共同写作方法很好地转移到了人类-LLM计划,而人类的参与仍然很宝贵。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We introduced CoWriter , a proactive agentic framework that shifts human-LLM co-authoring from passive text generation to an actively guided, methodical workflow. By adapting expert human writing methodologies, CoWriter leads the entire authoring process while actively eliciting user engagement. Our evaluation demonstrates that this approach significantly improves both the co-authoring process and the final output: CoWriter improved the overall writing experience, increased engagement and ownership, and produced documents preferred by authors, human annotators, and LLM evaluators over a strong control baseline. By demonstrating the value of proactive and methodical guidance, this work provides a foundation for designing user-centered agents and harnesses for a wider range of complex collaborative tasks.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了CoWriter,这是一个主动积极的代理框架,将人与LLM共同撰写的文本从被动生成转向积极引导,有条理的工作流程. CoWriter通过调整专家的人文写作方法,领导整个写作过程,同时积极吸引用户参与. 我们的评价表明,这种办法大大改进了共同编写程序和最后产出: CoWriter改进了总体写作经验,加强了参与和所有权,并编写了作者、人文注释员和LLM评价员所偏爱的文件,而不是一个强有力的控制基线。 这项工作通过展示主动和有条不紊的指导的价值,为设计以用户为中心的代理人和利用各种复杂的协作任务提供了基础。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Although the population size and demography is limited in our user studies (with recruitment conducted through universities for students and graduates), this is common practice in controlled NLP and HCI user studies.
Relatedly, the study scope was limited to a moderate number of writing topics (as is common in comparable studies).
Conducting large-scale controlled co-authoring studies is inherently expensive and time-intensive, as each session requires long interactive writing periods, extensive source materials, and detailed post-hoc evaluation. Such studies are particularly challenging to scale in academic research settings with limited resources and outreach. Nevertheless, the study was designed with counterbalancing across systems and topics, and combined user feedback, human document assessment, and automatic evaluation to provide multiple complementary perspectives on system behavior.
Broader deployment studies across more diverse populations, professional writing settings, and writing genres (e.g., expert or creative writing, where authors may prefer less guidance) would help further validate the generality of our findings and the significance of results.
blocks.zh:
尽管在我们的用户研究中人口规模和人口有限(通过大学为学生和毕业生招聘),但在受控制的NLP和HCI用户研究中,这是常见的做法.
与此相关的是,研究范围仅限于一些适度的写作专题(在可比研究中常见)。
进行大规模的有控制的合著研究本身费用高昂,而且时间很紧,因为每期都需要较长的交互式写作期、广泛的原始材料和详细的事后评价。 在资源有限和外联的学术研究环境中,这类研究尤其难以扩大规模。 尽管如此,该研究的设计在系统和专题之间进行了平衡,并结合了用户的反馈、人文文件评估和自动评价,以就系统行为提供多种互补的观点。
更广泛的部署研究涉及更多不同的人群、专业写作环境以及写作流派(例如,专家或创造性写作,作者可能倾向于较少的指导),将有助于进一步验证我们调查结果的普遍性和成果的重要性。

blocks.en: Our implementation used claude-sonnet-4.6 as the underlying LLM backbone. Some observed behaviors may therefore depend on characteristics of this specific model family. However, our work primarily studies co-authoring workflows, interaction design, and agentic behavior rather than model-specific capabilities. We therefore expect the proposed principles and workflow structure to transfer to other modern LLMs with comparable instruction-following and tool-use abilities.
blocks.zh: 我们的实施工作将Claude-sonnet-4.6作为LLM的基础支柱。 因此,一些观察到的行为可能取决于这个特定的模型家族的特点. 然而,我们的工作主要研究共同编写工作流程,互动设计,以及代理行为,而不是模型特定的能力. 因此,我们期望拟议原则和工作流程结构能够转移到具有类似指导跟踪能力和工具使用能力的其他现代有限责任公司。

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en: The study was approved by the institutional review boards (IRBs) of the participating universities. All participants provided informed consent prior to participation and were informed that they could withdraw at any time without penalty to their accumulated compensation. Participants were recruited via university-wide advertisements and were compensated according to local standards, independent of performance.
blocks.zh: 该研究得到了参与大学机构审查委员会的批准。 所有与会者在参加之前都提供了知情同意,并被告知他们可以随时退出,而无需对其累积补偿进行处罚。 学员通过全大学的广告招聘,并按当地标准获得报酬,与业绩无关。

blocks.en: Session logs, including interactions with the system and produced documents, were recorded with participant awareness for research purposes. All collected data was anonymized, and no identifying participant information is reported in this paper.
blocks.zh: 会议记录,包括与系统的互动和编写的文件,都为研究目的记录了与会者的意识。 所有收集的数据都是匿名的,本文件没有报告任何确定参与者的信息。

blocks.en: Participants were instructed that LLM-generated content may be imperfect and should be treated as assistive material requiring verification. However, the goal of the study was to evaluate collaborative writing behavior in a realistic setting. Therefore, imperfections in model outputs were expected and considered part of the experimental conditions rather than an anomaly. The resulting documents were created solely for experimental purposes and were not intended for external use.
blocks.zh: 与会者被告知,LLM生成的内容可能不完善,应作为需要核查的辅助材料处理。 然而,研究的目标是在现实的环境中评价合作写作行为. 因此,模型产出的不完善是预期的,被认为是实验条件的一部分,而不是异常。 由此产生的文件仅用于实验目的,并非供外部使用。

blocks.en: The study used academic source documents with appropriate licenses permitting their use in research. These sources did not contain sensitive personal information.
blocks.zh: 该研究使用了具有适当许可证的学术来源文件,允许将其用于研究。 这些消息来源没有包含敏感的个人信息。

blocks.en:
We used Claude Code as a coding assistant while developing CoWriter system and environment, as well as formatting and suggesting content for the paper.
We used ChatGPT 5.4 and CoWriter for assisting in paraphrasing some parts of the text while writing this paper to improve clarity and coherence.
Any use of AI was followed by manual verification and editing to maintain correctness and authenticity.
blocks.zh:
我们在开发CoWriter系统和环境的同时,还使用Claude Code作为编码助理,同时为论文格式化并提出内容建议.
我们使用ChatGPT 5.4和CoWriter来协助解释案文的某些部分,同时编写本文件,以提高清晰度和一致性。
在使用人工智能之后,进行人工核实和编辑,以保持正确性和真实性。

blocks.zh: 附录B 主要代理人(领导)

blocks.en:
Table 2: Tools exposed to the Leader (main) agent. All tool responses are formatted to text for easier consumption by the LLM.
The rules for usage of the tools are detailed in the system prompt ( Figure 28 ).
blocks.zh:

这些工具的使用规则详见系统提示(图28)。

blocks.en:
Figure 28 presents the full system prompt used by CoWriter ’s Leader agent.
It encodes the iterative workflow,
per-step invitations, the chat-message and citation conventions, and the tools available to the agent.
The tools of Leader are shown in Table 2 .
The shared document that Leader reads and edits is an XML tree (the “ <document> ” element is in Figure 6 ).
blocks.zh:
图28显示CoWriter的领头人代理人使用的全系统提示。
它编码了迭代工作流程,
每一步邀请、聊天信息和引用公约以及代理人可用的工具。
领导者的工具见表2。
Lead 读取和编辑的共享文档是 XML 树(“文档”元素见图6)。

blocks.en:
At the start of a co-authoring session, the underlying LLM is given the system prompt, and the agent greets with a predefined message to the user.
Upon a new user message or document update (triggered by Monitor ), the LLM receives the current document, the chat history (as a list of messages), the Writing Log , and a list of system reminders pertaining to the current state of the workflow (see example in Figure 6 ).
Accordingly, the LLM executes a ReAct loop ( Yao et al., 2023 ) , interleaving reasoning steps, tool calls, and ending by emitting a final chat message to the user.
blocks.zh:
在共同编写会话开始时,基础LLM被给予系统即时,代理商向用户发出预先定义的消息.
在新的用户信件或文档更新(由Monitor 触发)后,LLM收到当前文档,聊天历史(作为信件列表),写入日志,以及与工作流程现状相关的系统提醒列表(见图6中的例子).
因此,LLM执行一个ReAct循环(Yao等人,2023年),交互推理步骤,工具调用,最后向用户发送最后的聊天信息.

blocks.en:
When Leader is still processing a previous message, the event is queued until processing finishes.
When more than one event is enqueued, only the last may trigger the agent.
Concurrent document updates (by both Leader and the user) are handled with the Yjs protocol that manages concurrent updates to a shared data structure (the document) in a conflict-free approach ( Nicolaescu et al., 2015 ) .
We used the implementation from https://yjs.dev/ .
blocks.zh:
当lead仍在处理前一个消息时,该事件会被排队直到处理完毕.
当一个以上的事件被排列时,只有最后一个可能触发代理.
同时进行的文件更新(由领导人和用户共同进行)由Yjs协议处理,该协议以无冲突方式管理共享数据结构的同步更新(文件)(Nicolascu等人,2015年)。
我们利用了https://yjs.dev/中的内容。 。 。 。

blocks.en: Appendix D Monitor Details
blocks.zh: 附录D 监视器 细节

blocks.en: Figure 26 shows the Monitor ’s full system prompt, and Figure 7 depicts its per-event output scheme.
blocks.zh: 图26显示监测器的全系统速率,图7显示其每个活动的产出计划。

blocks.en:
Monitor observes a new event from the user (either a chat message or a document revision) and conditionally triggers Leader .
For user messages Monitor always triggers Leader . Whether to trigger on a user revision depends on its decision.
Next, Monitor sends Leader a message consisting of the event, the current system reminders, the current document XML ( Figure 25 ), and the Writing Log ( Figure 21 ) for the agent to act on.
Finally, Leader emits a message to the user, Monitor observes it, computes the next iteration’s system reminders (see Figure 7 ), and updates the Writing Log in the background (without adding latency or blocking the conversation).
blocks.zh:
监视器观察到用户的新事件(无论是聊天消息还是文档修改),有条件地触发lead .
对于用户信件监视器总是触发指令长. 是否触发用户修改取决于其决定.
下一步, 监视器发送 领导由事件、当前系统提醒、当前文件XML(图25)和代理行事的写入日志(图21)组成的信件。
最后,领导者向用户发送消息,Monitor观察,计算下一个迭代的系统提醒(见图7),并在背景中更新写入日志(不增加延迟或屏蔽对话).

blocks.en: If the response fails to parse, or if any old_text in a writing_log_replacements entry does not match the current Writing Log exactly once, Monitor self-corrects by re-issuing the prompt with the error appended (up to three attempts in total).
blocks.zh: 如果响应无法解析, 或者如果写入_ log_ 替换项中的任何旧的文本不能完全匹配当前写入日志一次, 监视自更正通过重新发布带有附加错误的提示( 最多三次尝试) 。

blocks.en: We followed a system-reminders pattern, as incorporated in the popular coding agent Claude Code. 7 7 7 https://claude.com/product/claude-code Specifically, Monitor wraps each user event (chat message or document update) with a list of system-reminders to notify Leader about the current state of the authoring process and on any open items for possible actions.
blocks.zh: 我们遵循了一种系统重复模式, 包含在流行的编码代理 Claude Code. 7 7 https://claude.com/produces/claude-code (中文(简体) ). 具体地说,Monitor将每个用户事件(聊天消息或文档更新)用一个系统提醒列表包裹起来,将作者进程的现状和任何可供操作的开放项目通知领袖.

blocks.en: Every Leader turn message ends with a <system-reminders> block (example in Figure 6 ) giving Leader a compact snapshot of the writing-process state. The block is partitioned into four labeled sections: • Status — the current writing activity and word count (computed) vs. target ( Monitor -inferred), plus code-computed signals: [TBD] / [outline] / [in-progress] progress markers in the document, broken citations (named <deeplink> in the prompts), and a flag set when the user has edited the document since Leader ’s last read. • Communication — open questions and open requests still awaiting a reply, each tagged with its direction ( from_user / from_agent ). • Pending — the next workflow steps from a fixed list of statements (e.g. Brainstorming not done , Sections not reviewed by user ). • Feedback — one concise, location-specific sentence flagging the most relevant non-obvious divergence from the Writing Goal or the recent chat, surfaced verbatim as the Monitor ’s steering nudge.
blocks.zh: 每个导师转动消息以一个 < system-reminders > 块结尾(例如图6)给导师一个紧凑的写进程状态快照. 块被分为四个标签部分: • 状态 – 当前写入活动和字数(computing) vs. target (Monitor - inferred), 加上代码计算信号: [TBD] / [outline] / [进行中] 文档中进度标记, 引用中断(在提示中称为<deeplink>) , 用户自 Leader 上次读完后编辑文档时设置的旗帜. • 通信——公开问题和公开请求仍在等待答复,每个问题和请求都按其方向(来自_用户/来自_代理人)标注。 待定——从固定的报表清单(如集思广益,用户未审查的章节)中采取下一个工作流程步骤。 · 反馈——一个简明的、针对具体地点的句子,标出与写作目标或最近聊天最不明显的差异,以逐字逐字的方式显示,它是监测员的指导方向。

blocks.en: Communication — open questions and open requests still awaiting a reply, each tagged with its direction ( from_user / from_agent ).
blocks.zh: 交流——公开问题和公开请求仍在等待答复,每个答复都按其方向标注(来自_用户/_代理人)。

blocks.en: Pending — the next workflow steps from a fixed list of statements (e.g. Brainstorming not done , Sections not reviewed by user ).
blocks.zh: 待定——从固定的语句列表(如集思广益未完成,各节未经用户审查)开始的下一个工作流程步骤.

blocks.en: Feedback — one concise, location-specific sentence flagging the most relevant non-obvious divergence from the Writing Goal or the recent chat, surfaced verbatim as the Monitor ’s steering nudge.
blocks.zh: 反馈——一个简明的、针对具体地点的句子,标出与写作目标或最近聊天最无关的不明显分歧,以逐字逐句的方式浮出水面,作为《监测》的指导。

blocks.en: The Monitor maintains the four system-reminder sections via per-field delta updates rather than regenerating them from scratch each turn ( Figure 7 ): null leaves the previous value unchanged, [] or "" explicitly clears, and any other value replaces.
blocks.zh: Monitor通过每个战地三角洲的更新来维护四个系统提醒部分,而不是从头再生成它们每个转弯(图7): 将以前的值保留不变,[]或""明确清除,任何其他值替换.

blocks.en: The four Status signals are code-computed signals recomputed on every Leader turn from the live document XML and source-file list: the current word count (whitespace-separated word count of the text); the progress-marker list using regex; the broken-deeplinks list (dangling citations to invalid sources or lines) validated against the source files; and the unread-user-edit flag (cleared the next time Leader reads the document).
blocks.zh: 四个状态信号是从SML和源文件列表中从当前文档XML和源文件列表的每个导师转动上重编的代码信号:当前单词计数(文本白空分隔的单词计数);使用regex的进度标记列表;针对源文件验证的断开深链接列表(向无效源或线条引用);以及未读用户编辑的旗帜(下次导师阅读文档时清除).

blocks.en: Appendix E Reviewer Agent
blocks.zh: 附录E 审查员 探员

blocks.en:
The Reviewer agent is invoked by Leader via the external_review tool call ( Table 2 ), optionally with a one-sentence focus hint that narrows the audience or review angle.
On invocation, the Reviewer runs a short ReAct loop ( Yao et al., 2023 ) over the Writing Goal and the current document XML, using the tools in Table 3 and the system prompt in Figure 27 .
The final assistant message is the review (Summary, Strengths, Issues, optional Coverage gap, Top fix) that Leader posts into the chat as a quoted block for both itself and the user to act upon.
An example output of Reviewer depicted in Figure 22 .
blocks.zh:
审查者代理通过外部_审查工具调用(表2)被领导者援引,可选用一个一判决焦点提示来缩小受众或审查角度.
在引用时,审查者使用表3中的工具和图27中提示的系统,在写入目标和当前文件XML上运行了一个简短的ReAct循环(姚等人,2023年)。
最后的助理信息是Lader将内容(摘要、强项、问题、可选覆盖面差距、Topfix)作为引用块张贴到聊天中,供自己和用户采取行动。
图22所描述的审查者的一个实例产出。

blocks.en: Table 3: Tools available to the Reviewer sub-agent. The Reviewer’s ReAct loop interleaves get_source_file lookups (to spot-check cited spans against the actual source lines) and a single final message that returns the structured review ( Appendix E ).

Figure 8 depicts the full writing-task definition presented to participants at the start of every writing session (§ 4.1 ).
The topic title (underlined) was instantiated with the participant’s assigned topic (one of the four topics in Table 4 ) while all other instructions were identical across topics and across the two systems ( CoWriter and the baseline).

图8说明了在每次写作会开始时向与会者提出的全部写作任务定义(第4.1节)。
专题标题(下划线)与参加者指定的专题(表4的四个专题之一)一并列出,而所有其他指示在专题和两个系统(CoWriter和基线)之间相同。

blocks.en: The Writing Task and Setup (simulated real-life setting) The writing topic: \smaller{1}⃝ • You are a popular blogger of a blog on everyday life topics. • You want to educate your readers based on research findings on the topic of the blog post, while following your perspectives on the most important aspects of the given topic. • The blog post will be based on facts from the sources and your perspectives of them. • You want to select the information that you think would be most interesting for your readers, and may be most effective for them in improving their life habits and choices. – These can cover key research findings, varying conclusions vs. open questions, and takeouts and recommendations. • You should include: – Your perspectives that you will develop after exploring the source documents and share what’s important to you about this topic. – Your personal examples and experiences for illustration (that you feel free to share anonymously, or with some variations). – Your opinion about the topic. • Audience: general audience • Tone: blog post with accessible language grounded in facts from the sources • Length: target 750-1000 words • Sources: Use only the 10 provided documents. Every non-trivial claim in the output document should cite relevant text from the sources that support it. The output should be grounded exclusively in the provided sources, not your prior knowledge. • Format: A blog post consisting of several paragraphs each with a heading including a final conclusion paragraph.

blocks.en: Appendix I User Study Questionnaires

blocks.en:
We developed the questionnaire statements to target our co-authoring process.
After each writing session, participants completed a per-system questionnaire of 37 statements rated on a 7-point Likert scale ( Table 6 ).
After completing both sessions, they completed a comparative questionnaire of 13 questions rated on a 5-point comparative scale ( Table 7 ).
The per-session questionnaire records each system’s rating in isolation, whereas the comparative questionnaire elicits a direct preference between the two.
Reporting both lets us cross-check absolute and relative judgments. Reverse-coded statements (marked in Table 6 ) were inverted to < 8 − score > <8-\text{score}> before analysis, so that a higher value always indicates a more positive response.
Each per-session questionnaire also included one instructional attention-check item, whose handling is described in Appendix J .
The per-session questionnaire additionally measured task load with NASA-TLX items ( Hart and Staveland, 1988 ) and usability with the four-item UMUX scale ( Finstad, 2010 ) .
blocks.zh:
我们编制了问卷说明,以针对我们的共同起草进程。

在完成了这两届会议之后,他们完成了13个问题比较问卷,按5点比较尺度评级(表7)。
每期调查表单独记录每个系统的评级,而比较调查表则直接引起两者之间的偏好。
报告两者都让我们交叉检查绝对和相对判断。 反向编码的语句(在表6中标注)在分析前被反转为 < 8 - 得分 > < 8-\ text{score},这样更高值总是表示更积极的反应.

blocks.en: Appendix J Attention-Check Handling
blocks.zh: 附录J 注意检查处理

blocks.en:
One participant (P6) failed an instructional manipulation check ( Oppenheimer et al., 2009 ) in both post-session questionnaires, giving the same wrong answer on both, consistent with item-level acquiescence rather than disengagement.
Within-session indicators showed strong engagement: structured task prompts, differentiated per-event quality ratings, and personal anecdotes integrated into both documents.
In a structured debrief, P6 accurately recalled both conditions and gave a detailed comparison of the two systems.
When asked which system to use next and which was more cognitively demanding, P6 chose the proactive system for future use, describing it as “writing with auxiliary wheels”. P6 identified the baseline as the more demanding of the two, reproducing the per-session direction under blind re-rating.
On the four-item Cognitive Load construct (1–7; higher = = more load), proactive = 1.00 =\mathbf{1.00} vs. baseline = 6.25 =\mathbf{6.25} ; on the four-item UMUX usability construct, proactive = 7.00 =\mathbf{7.00} vs. baseline = 6.50 =\mathbf{6.50} – both consistent with the debrief.
Following Curran (2016) on combining convergent indicators we retained P6 in the primary analysis.
blocks.zh:
一位与会者(P6)在两次会后调查问卷中都未能进行指令性操纵检查(Oppenheimer等人,2009年),对两者都给出了相同的错误答复,这符合项目层面的默认而不是脱离接触。
会期内指标显示出强有力的参与:结构化的任务提示、因事件而异的质量评级,以及将个人传闻纳入两份文件。
在有条理的汇报中,六主席准确地回顾了这两个条件,并详细比较了这两个系统。
当被问及接下来要使用哪个系统以及哪个系统在认知上要求更高时,P6选择了主动系统供未来使用,将其描述为"用辅助轮子书写". P6确定基线为两者要求更高的基准,在盲目重估下复制每场会议方向.
关于四项目认知负载构造(1–7;较高===增加负载),主动性=1.00 =\Mathbf{1.00}对基线=6.25 =\Mathbf{6.25};关于四项目UMUX可用性构造,主动性=7.00 =\Mathbf{7.00}对基线=6.50 =\Mathbf{6.50}——两者都与汇报一致.
继Curran(2016年)之后,我们在初级分析中保留了P6。

blocks.en: Appendix K Session Annotation Details
blocks.zh: 附录 K 会话注释细节

blocks.en: This appendix details the conversation annotations underlying the process metrics (§ 4.2 ), including the LLM procedure, human validation, and inter-rater agreement.
blocks.zh: 本附录详细介绍了作为进程衡量标准基础的对话说明(第4.2节),包括LLM程序、人类验证和双方协议。

blocks.en: We annotated each session message by prompting an LLM ( claude-opus-4.8 with high reasoning effort) once for each metric:
blocks.zh: 我们为每场会议的信息作说明,每个指标都发出一次LLM(Claude-opus-4.8, 并进行高度推理):

blocks.en: 1. Writing activities: The model labels each message with the single most prominent writing activity from the seven predefined activities ( Table 1 ), or “other” if none apply (prompt in Figure 23 ). 2. Engagement phrases: The model extracts every engagement expression verbatim from each message, classifying its type (question, choice, action request, or next-step proposal) and whether it was followed up (i.e., directly addressed in the collaborator’s next turn; prompt in Figure 24 ).
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 写作活动: 模型将每个信件标注在七个预先定义的活动(表1)中最突出的单一写作活动上,如果不适用,则标注“其他”(见图23)。 2. 约定短语: 该模型从每个消息中逐字抽取每个约定表达式,对其类型(提问、选择、行动请求或下一步建议)以及是否跟进(即合作者下一轮直接处理;图24中提示)进行分类。

blocks.en: Writing activities: The model labels each message with the single most prominent writing activity from the seven predefined activities ( Table 1 ), or “other” if none apply (prompt in Figure 23 ).
blocks.zh: 写作活动: 模型将每个信件标注在七个预先定义的活动(表1)中最突出的单一写作活动上,如果不适用,则标注“其他”(见图23)。

blocks.en: Engagement phrases: The model extracts every engagement expression verbatim from each message, classifying its type (question, choice, action request, or next-step proposal) and whether it was followed up (i.e., directly addressed in the collaborator’s next turn; prompt in Figure 24 ).
blocks.zh: 约定短语: 该模型从每个消息中逐字抽取每个约定表达式,对其类型(提问、选择、行动请求或下一步建议)以及是否跟进(即合作者下一轮直接处理;图24中提示)进行分类。

blocks.en: These message-level annotations (activity type, total engagement expressions, and successful follow-ups) are then aggregated per system to calculate the metrics in § 4.2 .
blocks.zh: 这些信件级说明(活动类型、总参与表达式和成功后续)随后被逐个系统汇总,以计算第4.2节中的衡量标准。

blocks.en: Two human annotators, both PhD students experienced in English academic writing, independently labeled 118 messages across four sessions (two per system) using the guidelines provided to the LLM. Human–LLM Cohen’s κ \kappa per message was reliable across writing activities ( κ = 0.62 \kappa=0.62 , unweighted), engagement expressions ( κ = 0.46 \kappa=0.46 , quadratic-weighted), and successful engagements ( κ = 0.55 \kappa=0.55 , quadratic-weighted), with an overall mean of κ = 0.54 \kappa=0.54 .
blocks.zh: 两位人文注释员,都是有英语学术写作经验的博士生,利用向LLM提供的准则,在四期(每个系统两期)中独立标注了118条信息. 人类-LLM 科恩每条消息的\kappa在写作活动中是可靠的(0.62\kappa=0.62,未加权),约定表达式(0.46\kappa=0.46,四重),以及成功的约定(0.55\kappa=0.55,四重),总体平均值为0.54\kappa=0.54。

blocks.en: This appendix details the human and LLM-as-a-judge evaluations of the produced documents (§ 5.3 ), covering the annotator pool, the self-review constraint, score aggregation, annotator instructions, and the complete questionnaire. Figure 10 and Figure 12 present the top five evaluation items with the highest average human and LLM preference for CoWriter , respectively.
blocks.zh: 本附录详细介绍了对所编制文件(第5.3节)进行的人的和即审即决的LLM评价,涵盖注释库、自我审查限制、分数汇总、注释员指示和完整的调查问卷。 图10和图12分别显示对CoWriter的人类和LLM偏好最高的前五个评价项目。

blocks.en:
Five annotators rated the 30 sampled document pairs.
Three of them had also participated in the writing study.
To prevent them from self-reviewing their own documents, each of these three did not rate any pair containing one of their own documents.
The remaining two annotators were external to the writing study and rated all 30 pairs.
blocks.zh:
5名注释员对30对文件样本进行了评级。
其中三人也参加了写作研究。
为防止他们自行审查自己的文件,这三种文件都未对含有自己文件的一对进行评分.
其余两个注释员是写作研究的外部人员,并对所有30对进行评分.

blocks.en:
While the evaluated aspects aim to be relatively objective, document-quality judgments naturally contain subjective components.
To reduce individual-rater bias, the score we report per pair and per item is the mean across the annotators who rated that pair.
blocks.zh:
虽然评估的方面力求相对客观,但文件质量判断自然包含主观成分。
为了减少个人评分偏差,我们每对和每件的评分是评分该对的注释员的平均值。

blocks.en:
For each pair, annotators were instructed to read Document A first and then Document B, and to carefully rate each sub-aspect.
They were encouraged to re-read either document as needed while answering.
blocks.zh:
对于每对,指示注释员先读A文档,然后读B文档,并仔细评分每个子谱.
他们被鼓励在答复时根据需要重新阅读这两份文件。

blocks.en: Annotators answered the same 19 comparative questions on every pair, grouped into four aspects taken from Lee et al. (2025) : interestingness , linguistic fluency , coherence , and logical fluency . Table 8 lists the full questionnaire.
blocks.zh: 注释者对每对都回答同样的19个比较问题,从Lee et al 分为四个方面. (2025年):有趣性,语言流畅性,一致性,逻辑流畅性. 表8列出了完整的调查问卷。

blocks.en:
We complement the human reader assessment (§ 5.3 ) with an automatic comparative assessment of all 48 document pairs (12 pairs per topic), each pairing one CoWriter document and one baseline document written on the same topic.
Three LLM-as-a-judge models scored every pair on the same 19 comparative questions and grouped into the four aspects.
The LLM-as-a-judge models used the same 5-point comparative scale given to the human annotators.
Each model was queried once per (pair, aspect) .
blocks.zh:
我们通过自动比较评估所有48对文件(每个专题12对),每对一个CoWriter文件和一个关于同一专题的基线文件,来补充人类读者评估(第5.3节)。
三个LLM-as-a-judge模型在同一19个比较问题上每对得分,并分为四个方面.
LLM-as-a-judge模型使用给人类注释者的同样的5点比较尺度.
每个模型(pair, side)都问过一次。

blocks.en:
The three judges were accessed through the OpenRouter API: 8 8 8 https://openrouter.ai/ openai/gpt-5.5 (version gpt-5.5-20260423 ), qwen/qwen3.5-397b-a17b , and deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro .
For all three judges the reasoning effort was set to high .
To control for position bias, a document written with CoWriter was placed in slot A for exactly 24 of the 48 pairs and in slot B for the other 24 (randomly assigned).
Full prompt for the judges is shown in Figure 13 .
blocks.zh:
三位法官通过OpenRouter API访问:8 8 8 8 https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-5.5(gpt-5.5-20260423版), qwen/qwen3.5-397b-a17b, 和 deepseek-v4-pro.
这三位法官的推理能力都很高。
为了控制位置偏差,用CoWriter写的一份文件被放在A槽中,48对中的24对,其他24对中的B槽中(随机分配)。
图13显示法官全速出庭。

blocks.en:
We assess citation correctness with the automatic citation-quality evaluation of LongCite ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) .
Each final document is segmented into sentences with PySBD ( Sadvilkar and Neumann, 2020 ) .
Every sentence is treated as a statement and paired with the source snippets its citations point to.
We then apply LongCite’s three citation-evaluation prompts.
The judge model was GPT-5.5 ( gpt-5.5-20260423 ) with reasoning effort set to high .
Citation length ( C ​ L CL ) is the mean number of words (counted with the NLTK word tokenizer 9 9 9 https://www.nltk.org/ ) in the cited snippets. Table 9 reports these metrics, with recall additionally split over statements that cite a source ( R cited R_{\text{cited}} ) and statements that do not ( R uncited R_{\text{uncited}} ).
blocks.zh:
我们通过对LongCite的自动引用质量评价来评估引用正确性(张等人,2025年)。
每一份最后文件都与PySBD(Sadvilkar and Neumann, 2020)一起被分解成句子.
每个句子都被当作一个陈述,并与来源的片段配对,以示引用。
然后,我们使用LongCite的三个引用-评价提示。
评委模型为GPT-5.5(gpt-5.5-20260423),推理努力定高 .
引用长度(CL CL)是被引用片段中的平均字数(与NLTK词代号器计算) 9 9 9 https://www.nltk.org/. 表9报告了这些衡量标准,并提醒说,在引用来源(R引用R_{\text{引用Q}})和不引用(R引用R_{\text{引用Q}})的语句中,还存在另外的分歧。

blocks.en:
This appendix complements the per-construct summary in § 5 with question-level breakdowns of the writer assessment. Figure 14 further details workflow adherence per writing activity and Figure 15 maps the transitions between them, while Figure 16 and Figure 17 detail the engagements by type and writing activity, respectively. Figure 18 and Figure 19 show per-system average ratings for the 37 per-system questions ( Table 6 ), and Figure 20 shows the distribution for the 13 comparative questions ( Table 7 ).
Per-question significance markers in both figures follow the paired t-test or Wilcoxon selection rule described in Appendix N . Table 10 reports the verbatim free-text responses to the two open-ended prompts of the per-system questionnaire.

本附录补充了第5节中按结构分列的摘要,对作者评估进行了问题分类。 图14进一步详细说明了每项写作活动遵守工作流程的情况,图15描绘了两者之间的过渡,而图16和图17则分别按类型和写作活动详细说明了聘用情况。 图18和图19显示每个系统37个问题的平均评级(表6),图20显示13个比较问题的分布情况(表7)。
这两种数字中的每个问题意义标记都遵循附录N所述的配对t测试或Wilcoxon选择规则。 表10汇报了对每个系统调查表的两个不限名额提示所作的自由文本逐字记录。

blocks.en:
For both the per-session and comparative constructs spanning more than one statement or questions, we computed internal consistency using Cronbach’s α \alpha .
per-system construct α \alpha spanned 0.65–0.89, indicating acceptable-to-good internal consistency.
Across the two multi-statements comparative dimensions α \alpha was 0.94 ( overall experience ) and 0.55 ( document self-expression ); the latter with a relatively lower α \alpha , yet all three of its forming statements yielded an identical + 0.93 +0.93 mean preference for CoWriter .

我们用Cronbach的α-α计算内部一致性,
α-α的每个系统构造范围为0.65-0.89,表明内部的可接受与良好一致性。
在两个多报表的比较维度中,α-α为0.94(总体经验)和0.55(文件自我表达);后者的α-α相对较低,然而其所有三个组成报表都得出了对CoWriter相同的+0.93+0.93的偏好。

Right: Percentage of sessions discussing each activity at least once, categorized by participation (both parties, agent only, or user only). While 54% of the baseline agent turns concentrate in localized reviewing & revising (vs. 29% for CoWriter ) with low agent involvement in early stages, CoWriter distributes the conversation more uniformly and successfully drives higher user participation across most writing activities.

Arrows indicate transitions between activities, labeled with their total counts. Activity nodes display the percentage of their incoming transitions that are adjacent (i.e., from an immediately preceding or succeeding activity). While both systems are iterative, each featuring over 30% backward transitions, CoWriter transitions are predominantly to adjacent activities (74% vs. 56% for the baseline; p = 0.015 p=0.015 ).

blocks.en: Appendix N Significance Testing
blocks.zh: 附录N 测试

blocks.en:
We compared per-construct composite scores between baseline and CoWriter using paired tests over the N = 14 N{=}14 within-subject pairs.
The “normality” of the paired differences was assessed via sample skewness and excess kurtosis, following West et al. (1995) , who treat violations as substantial only when | skewness | > 2 |\text{skewness}|\,{>}\,2 or | excess kurtosis | > 7 |\text{excess kurtosis}|\,{>}\,7 .
Under these thresholds all constructs except “Document Publish” (skewness = 2.28 =2.28 , excess kurtosis = 5.85 =5.85 ) fell within the mild range and were analyzed with a paired t t -test.
For Document Publish we instead report the Wilcoxon signed-rank test ( Wilcoxon, 1945 ) , which does not assume normality of the paired differences. Similarly, we applied this test to the workflow-adherence measures (§ 5.1 and Figure 2 ) as the goal-setting indicator exceeded the skewness threshold ( − 2.29 -2.29 ).
blocks.zh:
我们利用N=14 N{=}14的配对测试,比较了基线和CoWriter之间的结构复合分数。
在West等人(1995年)之后,通过样本skewness和过量的kurtosis对配对差异的“正常程度”进行了评估。 West等人(1995年)认为,只有在XQQ=2 text{skewness}|\,{>}\2或超量kurtosis|,|\7 text{过量kurtosis}|\,{>}\,{>}\7时,才将违规行为视为重大违规行为。 。 。 。
在这些阈值下,除“文件出版”外,所有构件(sewness = 2.28 = 2.28,超高的kurtosis = 5.85 = 5.85)都属于温和范围,并用配对 t - t - 测试法加以分析。
对于文件出版,我们报告Wilcoxon 签名排名测试(Wilcoxon,1945年),它并不假定配对差异的正常性. 同样,我们在工作流程遵守度措施(第5.1节和图2)中采用了这一测试,因为设定目标指标超过了Skewness阈值(−2.29-2.29)。

blocks.en:
We applied the same thresholds to the 37 per-question analyses.
Under them, only the engagement item “The system enabled me to use my choice of content during the authoring process.” exceeded the skewness threshold (skewness = 2.27 =2.27 , excess kurtosis = 6.51 =6.51 ), and we therefore report its result from the Wilcoxon signed-rank test ( p = 0.031 p{=}0.031 ).
blocks.zh:
我们对37个问题的分析采用了同样的门槛。
在它们下,只有“系统允许我在撰写过程中使用我对内容的选择”的项目超过了skewness阈值(skewness = 2.27 = 2.27,超额的kurtosis = 6.51 = 6.51),因此,我们报告Wilcoxon签名恶作剧测试的结果(p = 0.031 p = 0.031)。

blocks.en:
For the engagement rate (§ 5.1 ), we report an exact paired permutation test, enumerating all swaps of the system labels within each participant’s pair of sessions and recomputing the measured rate difference.
For the direction of transitions (§ 5.1 ), we computed, per session, the percentage of transitions to an adjacent activity, and compared the two systems with a paired t t -test over the 14 participants.
blocks.zh:
关于业务约定率(第5.1节),我们报告一个精确的对接通式测试,列举每个参与者的对会中所有系统标签的互换,并重算所计量的比率差。
就过渡方向(第5.1节)而言,我们按届会计算向相邻活动过渡的百分比,并将两个系统比作14个参加者的对t t测试。

blocks.en: Reviewer response: example Summary: This research-backed blog post argues that how we use our smartphones is more revealing than the devices themselves — working through six headed sections that cover phubbing’s relational toll, the loneliness-scroll feedback loop, the superiority of voice calls over text, and the distinction between purposeful and passive phone use. It supports each section with peer-reviewed citations while weaving in personal anecdotes and a "mirror" metaphor that the introduction promises and the conclusion returns to. The post is aimed squarely at a general adult readership with no assumed academic background. • Strength: \smaller{1}⃝ §4 ("Call. Don’t Text.") is the single clearest audience win — the personal confession ("I’m a chronic texter"), the oxytocin biology, and the closing epigram "Your voice is a hug. Your text is a sticky note." move from relatable self-deprecation to actionable science in one readable arc, realising the "weave in personal perspectives" goal more completely than any other section. • Issue 1 — §5¶1 ( #384237:L49 ): \smaller{2}⃝ The passive scrolling warning drops the source’s explicit scope qualifier — the cited line reads "exacerbate depressive symptoms in adolescent populations " — yet the document presents the finding as universal, implying it applies equally to all adult readers. Fix: add "particularly among adolescents and young adults" to the claim so it reads "can do the opposite — especially in adolescents and young adults," which is both accurate and still resonant for parents in the audience. • Issue 2 — §3¶1 (middle of "The Lonelier You Feel, the More You Scroll"): After a punchy reader-directed opener, three consecutive research-summary sentences arrive back-to-back ("Studies show that…" / "A 9-month longitudinal study confirmed that…" / "This trap hits hardest for shy personalities:") with no personal voice moment between them — the most academic-reading stretch in the post, and the point where a general reader is most likely to skim ahead. Fix: insert a brief second-person bridge before the shyness sentence, e.g., "Sound familiar? The longer the scroll, the harder it becomes to actually pick up the phone and call someone," to maintain the conversational register the surrounding sections set up. • Issue 3 — §4¶1 ( #202428:L59 ): The document says "students who leaned on texting over calling reported higher levels of loneliness and attachment anxiety," but the source at L59 compares "technology-based communication" (any digital channel) with telephone calls — not texting specifically. Naming texting as the culprit is slightly more precise than the evidence warrants. Fix: change "texting over calling" to "technology-based contact over phone calls" to stay faithful to the source’s actual category. • Coverage gap: \smaller{3}⃝ Source 532820 (Social Isolation and Smartphone Addiction) states at L43–45 that "loneliness and COVID-19 anxiety mediated the association between social isolation and smartphone addiction in both parallel and sequential ways" — meaning anxiety about the pandemic itself was a second independent driver , not merely a symptom of loneliness. The document collapses both into generic "loneliness and anxiety" in §3. For a post-pandemic general audience, a one-sentence nod — e.g., "Research found this loop intensified sharply during COVID-19 lockdowns, when anxiety about the virus itself became a second push toward the screen" — would make §3’s vicious cycle feel personally lived-in and timely, rather than abstract. • Top fix: Reinstate the "adolescent populations" scope qualifier on the passive scrolling claim in §5¶1 ( #384237:L49 ); it is the only place in the post where a source’s explicit population restriction is silently dropped, and a document that earns trust by promising every claim is cited can’t afford a quiet overgeneralisation that attentive readers or the author’s own peer circle might catch.
blocks.zh: 审查者的回应:实例 这个研究支持的博客文章指出,我们如何使用智能手机比设备本身更能说明问题, 它支持每个部分在编织个人传闻时进行同行评审引用,以及一个"迷信"的比喻,即引言承诺和结论回归. 该职位完全针对没有假定学术背景的普通成人读者。 • 力量:\small{1}§4(“呼吁,不要文字”)是最明确的观众胜出——个人忏悔(“我是一个慢性发音者”),催产素生物学,结束语缩写“你的声音是一个拥抱”。 你的文字是粘着的音符",从一个可读的弧形中可重塑的自我贬低到可操作的科学,比其他任何部分更完整地实现"从个人角度看重"的目标. • 第1期——第5章第1节(#384237:L49): \ small {2} 缩写 被动滚动的警告降低了来源的明确范围限定语——引言的一行是 " 青少年人口中的缓解抑郁症状 " ——但该文件将结论呈现为普遍性,意味着它同样适用于所有成人读者。 菲克斯:在主张中加上"特别是在青少年和青壮年中",因此其内容是"可以做相反的事情——特别是在青少年和青壮年中",这既准确,也仍然对观众中的家长产生共鸣. · 第2期——第3章第1节("孤独者你感受,你更滚滚"的中段): 经过一次猛烈的读者定向开机后,连续三句研究总结的句子相继出现("研究表明...... /"一个9个月的纵向研究证实..." /"这个陷阱对害羞的个性来说打击最大:"),他们之间没有个人的声音瞬间——在文章中读得最多的是学术的伸展,也是一般读者最有可能往前滑的一点. 修补:在害羞的句子前插入一个简短的二人称桥,如"听起来熟悉吗? 卷轴越长,就越难实际接通电话并给某人打电话",来维持设置的周围部分的谈话记录. • 第3期——第4章第1节(#202428:L59): 该文件称"依靠发短信而不是打电话的学生,报道的孤独度和附件焦虑度更高",但L59的源头将"基于技术的通信"(任何数字频道)与电话进行对比——而不是具体发短信. 将文字命名为罪犯比证据令略为精确. 固定:将"短信过电话"改为"以技术为基础的电话联系",以保持忠实于来源的实际类别. • 支助 覆盖范围差距:\smaller{3}⃝Source 532820(社会孤立和智能手机成瘾)在L43–45上表示,"孤独感和COVID-19焦虑以平行和相继的方式调解了社会孤立和智能手机成瘾之间的联系"——意思是对该大流行病本身的焦虑是第二个独立的驱动力,而不仅仅是孤独的症状. 文件在§3中同时崩溃成通用的"孤独与焦虑". 对于一个后流行的普通观众来说,一个一刑点点头——比如"研究发现这个循环在COVID-19封锁期间急剧强化,当时对病毒本身的焦虑成为了向屏幕的第二次推力"——将使§3的恶性循环感到个人生活和及时,而不是抽象. • 支助 顶点:在第5章第1节(#384237:L49)的被动滚动主张上重新列出“青少年人口”范围限定语;这是该文章中唯一一个静悄悄地放弃来源明确的人口限制的地方,
